scope: PROP-FLOOD-06.v4 (registry/proposals/flood_outlet_coping.json): one method-domain (M) proposal for a community flood-readout application (FloodConnect), via the governed proposals-lane intake process -- NOT promoted into registry/CANONICAL.json. Builds on the v3 ACK (C_H(U) no-pump-contradiction fix, graceful PARTIAL mode, promoter table adoption -- unchanged by this pass except where explicitly amended below). This v4 pass is driven entirely by round-2 independent review (REVIEW_PROP_FLOOD_06_r2.md, maker != checker, read-only review of the v3 commit), which found both changes below blocking MUST-FIX, no new founder instruction and no new external data. v4 AMENDMENTS: (1) round-2 MUST-FIX -- 'PARTIAL can silently outrank FULL, undocumented': v3's readout_classes.mode selection was exclusive (FULL consulted only the S_H/T_act bands via full_tier, PARTIAL consulted only the promoter table via promoter_max), so a unit with a fully-resolved ledger but a raw physical promoter fact (e.g. RAIN_24H_EXCEEDS_DESIGN firing) could report a LOWER tier than an otherwise-identical unit merely missing one input (hence PARTIAL) on the identical signal -- more data yielding a less urgent readout, nowhere stated as intentional. Fixed by making promoters a FLOOR under every mode: full_tier_v4 computes base_tier := max(band_tier, promoter_max) where band_tier is full_tier's S_H/T_act value if the ledger resolves (FULL) else L0 (PARTIAL/no-ledger contributes no band term, not a penalty), promoter_max is evaluated identically in every mode (not only PARTIAL), then the vulnerable-unit +1 rule applies to base_tier regardless of mode, then LR overrides the result entirely and ONLY fires iff cov(U) is entirely absent/stale, checked last. Proved monotone in Coq: full_tier_v4_promoter_monotone (for the same promoter table and ledger inputs, widening the coverage vector -- any cov component that was present stays present -- never lowers the tier, given the unit was not already LR, which is a refusal state excluded from this severity-monotonicity claim by hypothesis, not a counterexample to it) and full_tier_v4_full_ge_partial (for the same promoters and the same non-LR coverage, the FULL-mode tier is always >= the PARTIAL-mode tier the identical promoter inputs would give, since FULL only ADDS the band term into the same max, it never substitutes for the promoter floor). This is 'ข้อมูลเพิ่มไม่เคยลดระดับ' (more real data never lowers the reported level), stated and proved, not merely asserted; documented in the MD's new 'MUST-FIX #1' section and the JSON's readout_classes.mode field. (2) round-2 MUST-FIX -- 'coverage_score/mode are not structurally mandatory': v3's Coq full_tier_v3 returned a bare tier_level6, with mode/coverage_score/based_on/missing existing only as JSON/MD prose a consumer could silently drop, reproducing exactly the false 'normal' reassurance the founder's crisis-usability instruction (see the v3 “ข้อมูลเพิ่มไม่เคยลดระดับ” founder ruling already on file) was meant to avoid -- a real, checkable API-contract gap, not cosmetic. Fixed by making the Coq top-level return type a single inseparable `readout` record: { tier : tier_level6; mode : mode3; readout_coverage_present : nat; readout_coverage_total : nat; based_on : list input_kind; missing : list input_kind; promoters_fired : list promoter_id }, built from a fixed 7-field coverage_vector record (one bool per cov(U) component) and a promoter record list (id, requires, fires, level). Proved: readout_eq_dec (decidable equality of the whole record, via list_eq_dec lifted over the two finite enumerations input_kind and promoter_id), full_tier_v4_coverage_total_is_7 (coverage_total is exactly 7 by construction, tied to the 7-element all_input_kinds list, not a runtime-computed length that could drift), full_tier_v4_coverage_present_le_7 (coverage_present never exceeds 7, since it is a sum of 7 boolean-to-{0,1} terms), and full_tier_v4_LR_iff_coverage_present_0 (the record's own mode field equals M_LR iff readout_coverage_present equals 0). Mirrored in registry/proposals/flood_outlet_coping.json's new readout_classes.readout_schema field and the MD's 'MUST-FIX #2' section, both stating the mandatory consumer contract: tier MUST be rendered together with mode and coverage, never tier alone (FloodConnect's own UI copy: “ระดับ Lk · ข้อมูล n/7 · อิงจาก …”). coq/canonical/PROP_FLOOD_06_outlet_coping_tier.v extended with mode3/input_kind/promoter_id (finite enumerations, each with a proved eq_dec), coverage_vector and promoter records, full_tier_v4 (the new top-level function), the monotonicity helper lemmas (level6_to_nat_le6, nat_to_level6_spec, max_level6_mono_l/r, max_level6_ge_r, promote_one_mono/mono_if, promoter_max_monotone via a promoters_mono inductive relation, exists_true_component, coverage_present_pos_of_true, cov_all_absent_false_mono), and worked examples re-cast against full_tier_v4 (including a direct refutation of the v3 asymmetry: full_never_drops_below_partial_hatyai). Proposal bumped to v4 with a version_history entry, a new registry/LINEAGE.jsonl 'revised' row (code PROP-FLOOD-06), and a new honest_caveats entry recording the round-2 finding and its fix. No S_H/T_act band value, promoter threshold, or coverage-vector semantics is changed by this pass -- this is a mode-selection and return-type fix only. No claim about the Clay Millennium Navier-Stokes problem, or about any object's Clay/NS status, is made or implied anywhere in this change; the status of every existing Clay-related registry object (CANONICAL.json, coq/canonical/ pre-existing files, docs/CLAY_*) is unchanged.
